findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: url_preflight, read_url, site_status · Private data: url_preflight, domain_profile, domain_dns, domain_whois, domain_changes, domain_email_auth, ip_lookup · Public sink: domain_profile, domain_email_auth, bot_verify · Destructive: domain_trust.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: url_preflight, read_url, site_status · Private data: url_preflight, domain_profile, domain_dns, domain_whois, domain_changes, domain_email_auth, ip_lookup · Public sink: domain_profile, domain_email_auth, bot_verify · Destructive: domain_trust

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "bot_observatory" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
